IAMA senior Biology major graduating with honors. I'm also president of my school's Biological Honor Society, and have helped several of my professors with their research. Ask me anything!
what did you have for lunch today?
What area (s) of study interest you the most?

Animal cognition and Zoology in general. There's a lot of animals that are way more intelligent than we give them credit for, like a lot of birds and many mammals. That, and it's just fascinating to see how life survives and propagates itself with a variety of strategies in countless environments.
Do you feel that you are unique?

Not really. Most Biology majors are either looking to get into med school or trying to get a Ph.D and do research. It's honestly an incredibly formulaic degree path. You have to get involved in clubs if you want your CV to be competitive, so there's probably several thousand students just like me around the country.
When did you realize biology was your calling? Does it come easy to you or d you nee to study hard?

I originally thought I wanted to be a medical doctor, but after I took Zoology, I changed directions into Organismal/Animal biology. The animal world is just so interesting and cool. And I wouldn't say it comes easy to me, I have to try in my classes, but I feel like I have the right skill set to do well in it.

Yeah, it seems like a lot of people who like biology fall into the trap of med school because that's what they think they're "supposed" to do. Then they're exposed to research, and they realize it's much more interesting and rewarding. Happened to a lot of my classmates when I was in college, and I see it pretty often with my students now. Are you grad school-bound now?

I'm on the fence, personally. I was going to be, but some experiences have kind of disillusioned me towards academia in general. I'm likely going to go more into a government role, like Fish and Wildlife or Conservation biology
